leftEvidence.title: Pardon is granted while the unbelieving generation is excluded

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The LORD says, “I have pardoned according to your word,” yet declares that those who tested him and did not listen will not see the land.
points.right: The people despise the pleasant land, do not believe the LORD’s word, murmur in tents, and do not listen.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Caleb is singled out for another spirit and full following; Israel is told to turn toward the wilderness.
points.right: The LORD raises his hand to make them fall in the wilderness and scatter descendants among nations and lands.

payload.posture: Numbers explicitly says the people are pardoned and excluded; Psalm 106 foregrounds unbelief and the raised-hand judgment.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: The psalm remembers despising the pleasant land

payload.tension: Selective memory does not erase Numbers’ coexistence of pardon and sentence.
payload.title: Pardon beside the oath of consequence
